conclusion: A compact first-layer tip already supported by the bed must not seed a propagated sharp-tail tree when no raft is present. Use the existing 6 mm well-supported geometry threshold: if both first-layer bounding-box dimensions are at most 6 mm, do not propagate that initial tail; preserve elongated first-layer tails and raft behavior. Ordinary no-raft support skips the first object layer, while the legacy tree seeded that tip and propagated it into the extra right-side QQ tree. This scoped correction removes the right QQ trunk, preserves the necessary left trunk and contact paths, keeps test2 point-for-point identical including both complete bottom-contact outlines, and retains five earlier long unsupported paths with no interface-area change at or above Z 9 mm. It is a geometry-based rule, not model-coordinate filtering.
